heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 (Image Generation) and Seedance 1.5 Pro (Video Generation) — advanced foundation models developed by ByteDance for high-quality visual content creation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a full-bleed editorial hero with the headline on the left and a layered visual stack on the right rather than a standard split-panel. The right side should combine a large output preview, a smaller synchronized video card, and floating model chips over an orange mesh-gradient background. Keep the hero premium and business-ready with soft shadows, white result frames, and subtle grid-line decoration. The primary CTA must be solid Techjockey orange, with crisp white text, while the supporting proof band below the fold should shift into a dark section for contrast and credibility.

repetitionBreakers: Testimonials use spotlight cards instead of a grid
Pricing uses a centered comparison emphasis
Form lands as a floating conversion card
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | Enterprise AI Image and Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Create high-quality AI images and videos with ByteDance's Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Explore image generation, synchronized video and audio, trusted logos, pricing, and request a demo.

sections.backgroundTreatment: full-bleed orange editorial field with layered model-output cards, subtle interface shells, and compact benefit chips
sections.designNote: Make the hero content-first and continuity-driven. Headline must answer what it is; subheadline must answer who it is for; CTA must be the only action and read Get started. Include a short benefit row beneath the copy with AI image generation, AI video generation with audio, multimodal content creation, and enterprise-ready infrastructure. Keep the layout premium and dynamic without splitting into a heavy media-left composition.

Use a prominent logo-led proof band immediately after the hero. Because the input does not provide verified customer logos, substitute a clean 3-6 logo-style partner/enterprise reference grid only if real recognisable logos are available; otherwise use a compact metric strip. Keep this section visually calm to offset the loud hero and reinforce confidence early.

Treat the product area as two distinct spotlight modules with alternating emphasis, not a generic feature dump. First spotlight Seedream 4.5 with a preview-led panel and a supporting grid of the five capabilities. Then switch layout energy for Seedance 1.5 Pro using a darker or reversed visual treatment with a second preview panel and a compact feature stack. Avoid static flat card grids. Keep the focus on the 1-2 click-driving differentiators: high-resolution image quality, multimodal editing, synchronized audio-video generation, and cinematic motion control.

If included, keep this as a short trust-support section rather than a generic benefits block. Use 3-4 compact cards focused on buying confidence, evaluation support, and enterprise readiness. Make it visually lighter than products so it does not compete with the core model story.

Present pricing as a decision aid, not a marketplace catalog. Center the more business-critical option first and keep the layout concise. Use one highlighted card treatment with strong orange CTA buttons that all read Get started. Maintain strong spacing and avoid making this feel like a generic SaaS comparison table.

With 4+ testimonials, use a carousel-static spotlight treatment or a controlled 3-card emphasis, not a dense grid. Prioritize quotes from Creative Director, Video Producer, and Art Director to match the audience. Keep the section premium and editorial, with large quote marks and muted author details.

Finish with a strong conversion card that offers demo-oriented intent and visually feels like the final step. Keep it simple, high-contrast, and action-focused. The only button label must be Get started, and on mobile it should be full-width.

Use only if real recognised logos or credible media references exist. Do not use a moving marquee unless explicitly required. If no strong logo set is available, omit this section entirely and end at the form.

blueprint.designPersonality: Confident, editorial, premium, and business-ready — more like a polished creative platform than a futuristic lab. The page should feel trustworthy for enterprise buyers, with strong proof early, airy spacing, crisp cards, and intelligent contrast.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use high-end editorial AI visuals: polished prompt-to-output previews, device-safe mockups of image and video generation, layered model output cards, and motion-rich preview tiles. Avoid dark sci-fi styling. Use orange-on-white interface shells, premium product frames, and trust-heavy proof presentation. If logos are unavailable, replace with a metric strip rather than decorative placeholders.
blueprint.primaryGoal: Drive demo starts and evaluation requests for professionals comparing enterprise-grade AI image and video generation.
blueprint.recommendedHeroStyle: full-bleed editorial overlay with compact benefit chips and a single high-contrast CTA

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long and information-dense, so 40px keeps it readable while preserving hierarchy on a premium B2B hero.

colours.colourReason: Brand colors are locked to Techjockey’s provided palette. Orange becomes the signature action color, white and near-black provide contrast, and light grey is used for section separation.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-column hero with brand logo placement, large centered headline, short supporting copy, and a compact benefits list beneath. Uses strong top-of-page hierarchy and minimal distraction rather than a split-media hero.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Hero followed by a lead-capture/form block, then sequential product feature sections. Rhythm is linear and conversion-first with limited branching, no evident tabbed or accordion-based navigation.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Utility-led form card and content sections with rectangular containers, subtle borders, and practical spacing. Visual style is plain and business-oriented rather than decorative, glassy, or elevated-card heavy.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA is placed in the hero as the main conversion action; later sections use section-level request/demo-style CTA patterns. CTA strategy is sparse, focused, and not repeated as sticky or persistent elements.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer is not visible in the provided source; pattern cannot be inferred reliably.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: No large media panel or image-led storytelling in the observed structure. Visual communication appears text-forward with small iconography only.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Sequential feature blocks per product with section label, headline, descriptive paragraph, and bullet-style capability list. Supports progressive disclosure through stacked subfeatures rather than expandable controls.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form module directly after the hero. Form is built for B2B lead capture with multiple hidden tracking fields and a prominent card container, suggesting a high-intent conversion flow.
referenceMap.animationStyle: No clear motion system is evidenced in the markup; if present, it is likely limited to basic page scripts or third-party tracking rather than visible UI animation.

designNotes: Conversion-oriented B2B landing page structure with immediate lead capture.
Minimal ornamentation; content density is moderate to high and prioritizes clarity.
Visual hierarchy is driven by typography, section order, and CTA placement.

Do not make the page hero-only; full page must be visible and scrollable immediately

designStrategy.reasoning: This page is a solution-aware, high-intent enterprise-style landing page for two adjacent generative AI products aimed at creative and marketing professionals. The strongest conversion path is a clear, product-led narrative that quickly explains what each model does, why it matters, and how to get a demo or quote. Because the visitor trusts logos most, trust should be anchored by a prominent logo wall and subtle enterprise credibility cues rather than badge-heavy proof. The hero should be centered and message-led to accommodate the strong headline and avoid unnecessary media clutter, while the rest of the page should flow in a clean, linear sequence: trust, product one, product two, pricing, testimonials, footer. The structure should stay readable and practical, with balanced density and simple stacked feature layouts to avoid nested complexity.
